entries.title: DIY Product Photo Backdrops SO EASY!
entries.description:
Are you overcomplicating your backdrops?

You really just need two boards, and you can even make them yourself. (check out a previous post of mine to see how!) 

Super easy. Super gorgeous 🎉
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
One board lying flat on the table for your surface, one standing up behind it for your background. Push them together so there's no gap and you've got yourself a little set!

(and if you find you're getting shadows on the side opposite your light source, some white foam board with taped-on shelving brackets works wonders!)
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
My backdrops are MDF. I bought a 24" x 48" sheet and had them cut it in half at the store, so I came away with two 24" x 24" pieces. A light sand, two coats of Behr Marquee in matte with a small foam roller, and done.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
And here's the part I love 👇
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
Swapping ONE board changes the entire photo and vibes it a totally different vibe. Warm cream for the cozy shots, deep green for something moodier, plain white when you need it.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
So instead of buying a new backdrop every time you want a different look, you paint a board in a colour you love and you're set for years. They're sturdy, they don't crease like paper, and they photograph beautifully.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
Which colour would you paint first?

Here’s the setup 👇
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
1️⃣ Put a table by your biggest window. Clean surface on top, whatever you’ve got on hand. A painted board, a piece of fabric, a nice placemat.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
2️⃣ Set your product so the light comes in from the side rather than over your shoulder. Side light gives you shape and a bit of shadow, and that’s what keeps a product from looking flat.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
3️⃣ Turn off every other light in the room. All of them. Mixed light is what make your whites orange and your colours strange.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
And that’s it! No lightbox, no softbox, and best of all, no three-hour YouTube spiral.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
And if your best window happens to face north, even better. That’s the dreamiest, most consistent natural light you could hope for.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
Have you shot by a window using natural light? I’d love to hear how it went. 🤍

entries.title: 3 things you need to know for beautiful styled product photos
entries.description:
📸🌿3 things you need to know for beautiful, consistent, and effective styled product photos 👇

1️⃣ Your brand. Establish a brand identity (if you haven’t already), including aesthetics (colours, textures, materials), vibe (the overall feeling your brand gives off), and values (eco-friendly, heirloom, etc).

2️⃣ Your ideal customer. Hone in on just who the person is who’s most likely to buy your products and love what you create. Know as much as you can about them, especially what kinds of things would capture their attention in the noisy online space.

3️⃣ Your style guidelines. This is the fun part. Develop a shortlist of props and backgrounds that exude your brand and use them consistently for recognizable branded styled photos!

Photo styling is one of THE most fun and creative parts of product photography, and once you narrow in on those three things, it becomes SO easy and fun!

I'll show how you inside my online course, Stand Out & Sell: The Photo Styling Formula, available this week only!

Comment STAND OUT and I'll DM you the link. 💚

entries.title: 👻🎃SPOOKY SEASON PHOTO STYLING🎃👻
entries.description:
👻🎃SPOOKY SEASON PHOTO STYLING🎃👻

I don't know about you, but spooky season is my absolutely FAVOURITE. I love the crispy leaves, the cool air, and the ✨aesthetic✨

ESPECIALLY when it comes to my photos.

Here are some quick tips so you have your own fabulously spooktacular styled photos too!

🎃 Underexpose your photos slightly (you can use exposure compensation on any device to lower the exposure)
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🎃 Incorporate dark fabric for a dark + dramatic look
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🎃 Use a dark + moody Lightroom presets to add a sense of drama to the photo (my legendary presets are making a comeback soon - stay tuned!)
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🎃 Avoid fake fall leaves. Opt for real, and if you can’t find real in your area, incorporate rust-coloured dried flowers or plants instead
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🎃 Sure, the usual pumpkins are great BUT to really level-up your Halloween photo styling, include some less expected props like black candles, mini cauldrons, a black leather notebook, black lace, vials of dried herbs or black salt, etc
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🎃 And finally, have fun! Remember, photo styling is creative. Mix textures, include different elements, and play with arrangement

Wanna have beautiful photo styling for you product photos 365 days of the year? Then you'll LOVE my photo styling course, Stand Out & Sell: The Product Photo Styling Formula!

entries.title: Your products aren't the problem. Your photos are.
entries.description:
Your products aren't the problem. Your photos are.

Having high-quality product photos for your product business is non-negotiable. 

But taking these product photos doesn’t have to be complicated or expensive, and it doesn’t have to take forever! 

📸 ALL products can utilize product photography best practices. All products (jewelry, clothing, art, etc.) have nuances to how you should capture them. So no product is 'too different to fit the framework', because the framework is built for different.

📸 Fancy cameras and complex cameras aren't a requirement for great product photos. You just need to know how to get the most out of the tools you already have. 

📸 Your smartphone can be the tool, and your home can be the setting, for gorgeous, high-end photos. In small and questionably lit spaces, our students have taken stunning photos.

entries.title: DIY Photo Backdrop
entries.description:
This DIY is well loved, because it's SO much eeasier than you might think!
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
Make your own product photography backdrop with me!
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🪧 Get some MDF boards (smooth finish). I bought 24” x 48” and I had them cut in half at the store for two 24” x24” pieces.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🎨  Get some matte paint in your brand colours or whatever colour your like (the sample sizes work great!). I used Behr Marquee in matte finish.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🖌️  Sand the surface lightly then using a smaller foam roller, apply your first coat.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🖌️  Lightly sand with a fine sand paper before your second coat then apply your second coat with your foam roller.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
✅ And you’re DONE!
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
They’re perfect! Strong, durable, and they look fantastic in photos.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
If needed, you could prop them up with a chair, or try clamping the shelf brackets for a stronger support as well.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
Will you be giving this a try?

#photographydiy #diyphotobackdrop #productphotography
